## Summary

### Root cause (the bug class)
The tempting GC rule — *"drop a bottom-level tombstone when `seq < min(live snapshots)`"* — is insufficient. A bottom tombstone can be dropped while an **older version of the same key still lives in an un-compacted upper level**. The tombstone used to shadow that older copy for the latest read; removing it resurrects the old value (shadowing loss / key resurrection). Two secondary defects: overflowing the target budget instead of *choosing inputs*, and order-dependent merging of overlapping runs. I also found and fixed two verifier traps that mask real bugs: requiring preservation at *non-live* historical seqnos (GC is allowed below the oldest watermark), and tolerating duplicate `(key, seq)` pairs (impossible in a real LSM).

### Exact fix
A tombstone `t` is removed only if **all** hold: output goes to the bottom level; `t.seq < min(snapshots)`; and **no older version survives outside the compaction inputs** (`min_seq_outside[key] > t.seq`). When an older external version exists, `t` is retained but the entries strictly older than `t` inside the merge are still collapsed:

```python
if min_seq_outside.get(t["key"], INF) > t["seq"]:
    result.extend(group[:cut])        # safe: drop t and everything older
else:
    result.extend(group[:cut + 1])    # keep t, GC only older collapsed data
```

Plus: deterministic `(key asc, seq desc)` merge; greedy input selection so every step satisfies `bytes_out <= budget[to_level]`; `WA = Σbytes_out / Σbytes_in`; a fixed-point multi-pass scheduler (terminates because `Φ = Σ entries·(bottom − level)` strictly decreases).

### Verification (all passing)
```text
python3 test_lsm_cases.py        -> all deterministic edge cases passed
python3 test_lsm_planner.py 20000 -> OK 20000 randomized manifests verified
deep fuzz (4 levels, 30000)       -> OK
python3 lsm_planner.py manifest.json --verify -> verification {'ok': True}
```
The demo shows 3 ordered steps (`L0→L1`, `L0→L1`, `L1→L2`), GA of `d@5` (below watermark, reached bottom) while retaining `b@24` (above watermark), write amp `132/149 = 0.8859`, and no snapshot/latest resolution changes. The markdown contains the full proof sketch (inductive invariant over steps) and an appendix with the complete planner, edge-case suite, and fuzzer.

signatures.description: Build a leveled LSM compaction planner over an on-disk manifest (per-SSTable key range, sequence number, size) that performs one-level-at-a-time vertical compaction into leveled targets. A tombstone may only be dropped when its sequence number is strictly below every live read-snapshot watermark and it reaches the bottom level, the target level's size budget must be met by choosing which files to include (not by overflowing), overlapping input key ranges must be merged deterministically, and the planner must report write amplification as bytes_written/bytes_ingested. Given manifest.json plus a list of live snapshot sequence numbers, emit the ordered compaction plan (inputs, outputs, bytes_in, bytes_out) and the surviving tombstone set, and prove no snapshot-visible key or newer-version shadowing is lost.
